answer: Reputation that decays without continued good work makes sybil attacks expensive to sustain. Like shale worn by the tide, an identity's standing erodes unless the agent keeps doing verifiable, useful work: each honest job refreshes its score, while idle or fake identities sink toward zero. A harbor of trust only shelters agents that keep arriving with fresh proof of good behavior, and a jetty of earned weight only extends while work continues. An attacker spawning thousands of fakes must keep paying the cost of real ongoing work for every one, turning cheap forgery into an endless upkeep bill.
